title.narrative: Capacity-Building for Togo's peacekeeping operations training center in improvised explosive device (IED) risk management

description.narrative: The spillover of the security crisis in the Sahel onto coastal countries is having a significant impact on the latter, including Togo. Violent extremism and other threats linked to trafficking of all kinds (drugs, human beings, underground resources, recruitment of young people, etc.) are spreading very rapidly, with very serious consequences for the population. Non-state armed groups use a variety of means to carry out severe attacks against defense and security forces. They are increasingly using improvised explosive devices against security forces and civilians, causing severe loss of life and material damage.This project aims to provide Togos Peacekeeping Operations Training Centre (CEOMP) with additional capacity to train troops before they are deployed on peacekeeping missions. Through this project, the CEOMP will equip military and police personnel with the technical skills needed to recognize and detect improvised explosive devices. The aim is to prevent accidents and better protect the population.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
